newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials sees 32 pct sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials sees 32 pct sales growth.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc expects further gains in market share and sales growth to continue at a compound annual rate of about 32 percent, fueled by accelerating demand for semiconductors, its chief financial officer said on Monday.
"Our opportunities have never been better," Gerald Taylor said at the Robertson, Stephens technology conference in San Francisco.

Applied's strategy of broadening its product line to supply all types of equipment needed to process semiconductors was bringing in large chunks of business because customers want to buy from one supplier, the CFO said.
Taylor reiterated Applied's forecast that revenues this year should reach $3.6 billion.

He said the increasing semiconductor content found in the average electronic device suggested further acceleration in the demand for the equipment used to make chips. Typically 19 percent of the value of an electronic device reflects its semiconductor content, up from three percent 20 years ago, he said. And more and more devices have electronic components.

In the immediate future, opportunity lies in the semiconductor industry's turn to 0.25 processing technology. He said a rapid move to 0.25 processing had begun, though most of it has yet to be bought.
